S58.01.needs: a Free or paid account; a workspace admin account for the workspace MCP list
S58.01.note: Connectors may show as "coming soon" when the release lock is on (apps/web/features/connectors/lib/connector-release-lock.ts).
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and click Connectors.
Look for the "Your custom connectors" section and the other connector sections in the list.
Compare with Expected: the list shows the servers configured for the account.
For a workspace view, open the workspace console, click MCP servers, and look at the "Published MCP servers" list.
S58.01.where: Settings > Connectors (the list shows the section heading "Your custom connectors" and the Installed and Popular sections). Also: Workspace console > MCP servers, which lists "Published MCP servers".

S58.03.note: The desktop settings (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/DesktopCloudSettingsModal.tsx) use the same add flow; the exact field list for the form was not fully traced.
steps: Sign in, open Settings, and click Connectors.
Click Add, then click Add custom connector.
Type the server address in the field labelled Connector URL, and fill the name if asked.
Click Add.
Compare with Expected: the new server appears under "Your custom connectors" and can be used in chat.
S58.03.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Add custom connector

S58.06.needs: a token or an OAuth client from the server owner; a sign-in window is opened for OAuth
S58.06.note: Exact text of the token and OAuth field labels was not found; the secure storage behaviour is not checked here.
steps: Open Settings > Connectors and click Add > Add custom connector.
Enter the server URL, then fill the token or the OAuth Client ID and Secret fields if the form shows them (Advanced settings in the desktop app).
Click Test and save for an API-key connector, or follow the sign-in window for OAuth.
Compare with Expected: the connector shows as connected, and the secret is not shown again in the form.
S58.06.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Add custom connector (token or OAuth client fields); for an API-key connector, Settings > Connectors > [connector] > Test and save

S58.07.needs: a key or token for the server, or an OAuth sign-in
S58.07.note: For a custom MCP server the test is the sign-in or capability check after adding it; the separate test button was found only for API-key connectors.
steps: Open Settings > Connectors and click the connector you want to check.
Enter its key or token and click Test and save.
Wait while the button shows Testing the key.
Compare with Expected: a success message starting with "Connected." appears, or an error explains why the test failed.

S58.08.needs: a connected MCP server that has tools
S58.08.note: Empty-state and error wording were not confirmed against the live panel.
steps: Open Settings > Connectors and click a connector that is connected.
Scroll to the capabilities panel and find the section titled Tools.
Compare with Expected: the connector's tools are listed.
If the list is empty, look for the discovery error text instead.

S58.09.needs: a connected MCP server that offers resources
S58.09.note: Attaching a resource to a chat was not found in the code reviewed, only browsing; the resource list is also mounted separately as McpResourceList.
steps: Open a connected connector in Settings > Connectors.
Scroll to the section titled Resources.
Click a listed resource to look at it.
Compare with Expected: the server's resources are listed and can be opened.

S58.10.needs: a connected MCP server that offers prompts
S58.10.note: The code reviewed shows the list; running a prompt from it was not confirmed.
steps: Open a connected connector that offers prompts.
Scroll to the section titled Prompts.
Look at the listed prompts, and at the Templates section if the server offers templates.
Compare with Expected: the prompts appear and the user can pick one.

S58.11.note: Extensions are not shown as a separate section in the code reviewed.
steps: Open a connected connector in Settings > Connectors.
Read the capability panel: the Protocol row shows the MCP version, and the panel lists Tools, Resources, Templates and Prompts.
Compare with Expected: protocol, tools, resources and prompts are all visible.
Extensions were not found as a section.

S58.12.needs: a connected server that has been called for the log to show entries
S58.12.note: Logs are read from the call log endpoint; the health states are shown as text labels.
steps: Open Settings > Connectors and look at the Connector health section.
Read each connector's state: Responding, Degraded, Not responding or Not called yet.
Click a connector, then click Tool permissions, and scroll to Recent calls.
Compare with Expected: the health state and the recent call list (or an empty message) are shown.
S58.12.where: Settings > Connectors > Connector health; and Settings > Connectors > [connector] > Tool permissions > Recent calls

S58.13.note: The + button's exact visible label was not confirmed; the Connectors row text is taken from ComposerPlusMenu.tsx.
steps: Open a chat and click the + button in the composer (aria label More composer options).
Click the Connectors row.
Switch a connected connector's toggle off, then check it is off.
Switch it back on and compare with Expected: the connector is disabled without being removed, and re-enabled.
S58.13.where: Chat > composer + menu > Connectors > toggle a connector row

S58.15.needs: a workspace admin account and a second member account to see the result
S58.15.note: Connector releases are gated by assertConnectorsReleased on publish.
steps: Sign in with a workspace admin account and open the workspace console.
Click MCP servers.
Click Publish to everyone on a server, then check the list shows Published to everyone.
Compare with Expected: the approved list is visible to members; retiring asks for confirmation first.
S58.15.where: Workspace console > MCP servers (the approved list uses Publish to everyone, Unpublish and Retire for everyone)

S58.17.needs: a connected MCP server that ships an app UI
S58.17.note: The card's visible title was not confirmed.
steps: Open a chat with a connected MCP server that ships an app and ask the assistant to use it.
Look for the app card inside the reply.
Compare with Expected: the app renders as an interactive panel in the chat.
If it fails, read the error text.
S58.17.where: Chat > a reply that shows a connected app card (it appears after the assistant uses an MCP tool that ships an app)

S58.18.note: The handshake is not visible; only the success or failure of the card is.
steps: Open a chat reply that shows an app card.
Wait for the app to load and show its content.
If the handshake fails, the card shows the error MCP App failed to load instead.
S58.18.where: Inside the app card in chat; the handshake itself has no control

S58.19.note: Theme and display mode were not confirmed visually.
steps: Open a chat reply that shows an app card that uses a tool result.
Check that the app shows the data from that tool result.
When it asks to run a tool, read the sentence This App wants to run followed by the tool name.
S58.19.where: Inside the app card in chat; the host passes data to the app with no control of its own

S58.20.needs: a connected MCP app that asks for a tool call
S58.20.note: Resource reads through the host were not seen as a separate control.
steps: Open a chat with a connected app card that asks to run a tool.
Read the message This App wants to run followed by the tool name.
Click Allow once to approve that one call, or Deny to refuse it.
Compare with Expected: the approved call runs through the host, and a denied call is refused.
S58.20.where: Chat > app card > approval prompt (This App wants to run [tool name]) > Allow once or Deny

S58.21.needs: a connected MCP app that asks to resize
S58.21.note: The size limits were not confirmed on screen.
steps: Open a chat reply that shows an app card that changes size.
Watch the card height change as the app loads or its content changes.
Check that the card stays within a limit and does not take over the whole chat.
S58.21.where: Inside the app card in chat; the height changes with no control

S58.22.needs: a signed-in account and a connected MCP app
S58.22.note: Credentials are handled by the server route apps/web/app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/mcp/route.ts, not by the card.
steps: Open a chat reply that shows an app card that calls a server tool.
Use the app and check that it does not ask for a password or token.
Compare with Expected: the actions run as the signed-in user.
S58.22.where: Inside the app card in chat; the app uses the signed-in user with no credential prompt

S58.23.needs: a second account in the same workspace
S58.23.note: The payload route is apps/web/app/api/mcp-apps/payload/[payloadId]/route.ts; the viewer check was not traced fully.
steps: Sign in as user A and open a chat with an app card; note what it shows.
Sign in as user B (a second account) and open the same app payload.
Compare with Expected: user B does not see or act on user A's payload.
S58.23.where: Inside the app card in chat; access is checked on the server for each viewer

S58.28.needs: a connected MCP server that has a version or schema mismatch, if one is available
S58.28.note: The exact wording for a version mismatch or partial support was not found; only the Protocol row and rejected-tool reasons were.
steps: Open a connected connector in Settings > Connectors.
Read the Protocol row and the MCP version it shows.
Look for any rejected tools with a reason in the capability panel.
Compare with Expected: a version or partial compatibility problem is reported for the server.
S58.28.where: Settings > Connectors > [connected connector] > the Protocol row in the capabilities panel
